subject: VAL
label: Grade 01
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 01 Values and life skills, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Kindness and sharing
modules.outcome: show kind actions and say why they matter
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Kindness and sharing', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: show kind actions and say why they matter. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen and talk: hear a short story, text or example linked to 'Kindness and sharing' and say what it means in your own words.
Connect: name one place in your own day where it applies.
Use it: show kind actions and say why they matter. Practise with care and respect, in class and at home.
Reflect: what went well, what was hard, and one thing you will do next time.
modules.example: Solved: A classmate drops books. Kind action: help pick them up and say 'Are you OK?'. Reflect: how did it feel for them, and for you? Method: Model run for 'Kindness and sharing'. A short text or story is read aloud. Learners say the main lesson in one sentence. In pairs they find one moment in school or home where this lesson would help. Each learner plans one small action for the week and tells it to a partner. At the end of the week they report back. What a good answer looks like: the lesson is in the learner's own words, the example is real and local, and the action is small enough to do. Content follows the approved local syllabus and is checked by a qualified teacher.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Show kind actions and say why they matter: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, The situation: At break, Zaid has two biscuits. Maryam sits next to him and has none because she forgot her lunch box. Zaid notices she is looking at the floor and is very quiet.

Step 2, Notice feelings: Zaid asks himself, 'How does Maryam feel?' Her shoulders are down and she is not talking, so he thinks she is sad and hungry. Noticing how someone feels is the first step of kindness.

Step 3, Choices: Zaid sees three choices. He can eat both biscuits, eat one and hide the other, or give one to Maryam. He thinks about how each choice would make Maryam feel and how it would make him feel.
Step 4, The kind choice: Zaid says, 'Maryam, would you like one of my biscuits?' She smiles and says, 'Thank you!' He now has one biscuit and she has one. Two children are eating, not one.

Step 5, Why it matters: Zaid still has one biscuit, so he lost only a little. Maryam gained a lot, because she was hungry. Sharing makes both children feel warm, and Maryam may share with someone else another day.

Step 6, Say it: Zaid finishes the sentence, 'It is kind to share because it helps a friend who needs it.' Kind actions are things you do, like giving or helping, plus kind words like please and thank you.

Your turn: Sara has one pencil and Hamdan has none during writing time. What can Sara do and why? Model answer: Sara can lend the pencil first or share by taking turns, because Hamdan needs it now and sharing helps him write and feel included.

ladder: L1: kindness, honesty and sharing in daily life.
L2: responsibility, courage and care for others and nature.
L3: fairness, respect for difference and service.
L5: leadership, wellbeing and ethical reasoning.
L6 (degree): applied ethics, culture and community work.
L7 (postgraduate): scholarship, counselling or teaching at depth.
